terminal_name: Mayaguez / Yabucoa proposed ship-based LNG import terminals (PREPA IRP)
issue: PREPA's 2019 Siemens IRP 'preferred plan' (ESM scenario) proposed NEW ship-based LNG import terminals at Mayaguez and Yabucoa alongside CCGT conversions (~302 MW each, ~$1B gas-port capex). Puerto Rico's Energy Bureau REJECTED this in its 2020 IRP Final Resolution and Order as economically unjustified (not selected by optimization modeling in any other scenario). Current status (2025-2026): Yabucoa's aging Frame-5 peaker units are being DECOMMISSIONED in favor of a PREB-approved (Feb 2024) 40 MW battery storage system -- the Yabucoa LNG-terminal concept is superseded, not merely dormant. Mayaguez's Feb-2025 NEPR-conditional approval to convert its diesel units to natural gas is supplied via the existing San Juan terminal/NGSPA framework (see the power_plants_supplied finding above) -- no new marine import facility at Mayaguez has been permitted, sited, or funded as an independent project. SCOPE DOUBT RESOLVED (per CLAUDE.md/Discovery SOP: resolve before staging, never stage-with-doubt): neither candidate meets the concrete-step threshold for a new terminal today. Not staged as new_terminal or monitor_list. Documenting here so a future discovery pass does not re-surface this IRP-era planning-document proposal as a fresh lead without first checking whether the underlying IRP cycle has reopened it. Leads: rmi.org/puerto-ricos-electricity-system-at-a-crossroads/, sanjuandailystar.com 'Genera PR submits plan to decommission Yabucoa peaker units', energia.pr.gov IRP 2019/2020 dockets (AP20180001).
suggested_action: No staging action this batch. If a future PREPA/PREB IRP cycle re-proposes a Mayaguez or Yabucoa marine LNG terminal with an actual permit/siting/FEED step, re-open as a discovery candidate.
